“For I have given you an example,
that you should also do as I have done to you.”
Key points:
1. Greet the congregation and explain that today is the first of the Three Foundations.
2. The Three Foundations: Jesus is my role model, the Bible is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide.
3. Key verse: John 13:15; supporting verses Philippians 2:5 and Matthew 7:24.
4. Set the tone in one sentence: Jesus is not only Saviour but role model.

brief12.title: Introduction · Where Is Your House Built?
notes: Slide text:
The Tower of Pisa has leaned for over 800 years
The problem is not the carving but the foundation
Fervent faith, but no foundation
When the storm comes, we begin to lean
Key points:
1. Illustration: the Tower of Pisa, begun in 1173, began to lean at the third storey; the foundation was only about three metres deep, with soft clay and fine sand beneath.
2. Closed in 1990 over safety concerns, it reopened in 2001.
3. Application: tall and handsome above ground, but only three metres deep below.
4. The lean didn’t happen in a day; it started at the third storey.

brief12.title: Key Verse and Background
notes: Slide text:
The night before Passover, Jesus washes the disciples’ feet
He lays aside his garments and wraps a towel around his waist
“I have given you an example” (John 13:15)
Example = a demonstration set before your eyes
Key points:
1. Quote the two foundations of Matthew 7:24–27: the difference is not in the hearing but in the doing.
2. Background: John 13 begins “the Book of Glory”; John 13:3–5, Jesus lays aside his garments and wraps a towel around his waist.
3. Culture: foot-washing was a slave’s job; the disciples had just argued about who was greatest (Luke 22:24).
4. Original language: “example” is ὑπόδειγμα, a demonstration set before your eyes; 1 Peter 2:21 uses ὑπογραμμός, a copybook for tracing.

brief12.title: 1. The Foundation Is Not Experience or Tradition
notes: Slide text:
Experience is precious but subjective
Elijah: asking to die after Carmel
Tradition has value but is not always right
“Hold tightly to the tradition of men” (Mark 7:8)
Key points:
1. Elijah: fire from heaven in 1 Kings 18; asking to die under a juniper tree in 19:4. Yesterday’s fire can’t burn up today’s fear.
2. Psychology: Loftus and Palmer’s 1974 study — the wording of a question can rewrite memory; people even remembered broken glass they never saw.
3. Tradition itself is not the enemy (2 Thessalonians 2:15); the problem is putting tradition where Jesus belongs.
4. Mark 7:8 and 7:13; the Pharisees were the most earnest, yet did not recognise the Son of God.

brief12.title: Jesus Alone Is the Unshakeable Rock
notes: Slide text:
“No one can lay any other foundation
than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.”
(1 Corinthians 3:11)
From the temporary perspective to the eternal
Key points:
1. 1 Corinthians 3:11; 10:4, “the rock was Christ.”
2. Hebrews 13:8, Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.
3. Hebrews 12:2, “the author and perfecter of faith”: “author” is ἀρχηγός, the commander leading in front; “perfecter” is τελειωτής, the one who brings a thing to completion.
4. The 321 shift of perspective: from man’s to God’s, from the earthly to the heavenly, from the temporary to the eternal.

brief12.title: The Life of Jesus · The Pattern of the New Self
notes: Slide text:
Put away the old self, put on the new
Be renewed in the spirit of your mind (Ephesians 4:22–24)
The new self is created in the likeness of God
Copy the original — Jesus — every day
Key points:
1. Read the whole of Ephesians 4:20–24; “put away” and “put on” are the verbs of changing clothes, and between them is “be renewed in the spirit of your mind.”
2. The image of God is seen in Jesus: Colossians 1:15, Hebrews 1:3, John 1:14.
3. Romans 8:29, predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son.
4. Illustration: painters copying a master’s original; the Louvre has run a copyists’ programme since the late eighteenth century.
5. Science: Bandura’s 1961 Bobo doll experiment and his 1977 Social Learning Theory; Rizzolatti’s team discovered mirror neurons in the early 1990s.

brief12.title: The Teaching of Jesus · Learn from Me
notes: Slide text:
“Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me”
(Matthew 11:29)
“Just as I have loved you, you also love one another”
Love, forgiveness, humility, obedience, mercy
Key points:
1. Read the whole of Matthew 11:28–30; “learn from me” is literally “learn from me,” and “disciple” (μαθητής) means “someone who is learning.”
2. Mark 1:17, “Come after me”; in the first century, following a rabbi meant living with him and being covered in the dust of his feet.
3. The new commandment of John 13:34–35: the standard is Jesus himself.
4. These qualities are the DNA of God’s system; the ninefold fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22–23 links to the 920 practice.

brief12.title: Have the Mind of Christ Jesus
notes: Slide text:
“Didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied himself” (Philippians 2:6–7)
Satan says: I will make myself like the Most High
Humility overcomes pride; selflessness overcomes Satan
Key points:
1. Read the whole of Philippians 2:5–11; “have this in your mind” (φρονέω) is the orientation of the mind — precisely a change of mindset.
2. The staircase going down: existing in the form of God, not grasping, emptying himself, the form of a servant, the likeness of men, humbling himself, obedient to death, death on a cross.
3. Explain that emptying himself does not mean emptying out his deity, but not treating equality with God as a privilege to hold on to.
4. Set beside the five “I will”s of Isaiah 14:13–14: Satan grasps upward; Jesus walks downward.
5. A line generally attributed to Bonhoeffer’s The Cost of Discipleship: “When Christ calls a man, he bids him come and die.”

brief12.title: Don’t Let People Replace Jesus
notes: Slide text:
No ministry model in place of Jesus’ pattern
No leader’s style hiding the face of Jesus
No spiritual experience in place of Jesus’ words
“They saw no one, except Jesus alone” (Matthew 17:8)
Key points:
1. The bronze serpent: commanded by God in Numbers 21:8–9; broken by Hezekiah in 2 Kings 18:4 because people burned incense to it.
2. Acts 14:14–15, Paul tore his clothes; Revelation 19:10, the angel said, “Don’t do it!”
3. John 6:26, you seek me not because you saw signs but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
4. The Mount of Transfiguration: Matthew 17:5, “Listen to him”; 17:8, lifting up their eyes they saw no one but Jesus.
5. Psychology: Asch’s conformity experiments in the 1950s and Milgram’s obedience-to-authority experiments in the early 1960s; 1 Corinthians 1:12–13.

brief12.title: Putting It into Practice · Three Actions
notes: Slide text:
Read the Gospels daily; watch what Jesus does
In conflict, ask: what would Jesus do?
Remind one another with a spiritual companion
Practise again and again until it becomes habit
Key points:
1. Practice 1: the four Gospels have 89 chapters; read one a day and walk through Jesus’ whole life in three months.
2. Practice 2: Charles Sheldon’s In His Steps (1896), the source of WWJD; compare with the Gospels rather than guessing from imagination.
3. Practice 3: 235 relationships, asking each other three questions every week; 1 Corinthians 11:1, be imitators of me as I am of Christ.
4. The eight stages: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication.
5. Data: Lally’s team (2010) found a new habit takes 66 days on average, ranging from 18 to 254 days.

brief12.title: Closing and Call
notes: Slide text:
Jesus is the starting point of our faith
And the model for our whole life
Set your heart: follow Jesus all your life
Let Jesus be King and receive all the glory
Key points:
1. Take him only as Saviour and we live as a forgiven old self; take him as role model and we live as a renewed new self.
2. Return to the opening: the tower’s foundation could not be laid again, but our lives can.
3. Quote John 13:15 again and call people to set their hearts.
4. The Two Core Values: let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory.

brief12.title: Prayer of Response and Blessing
notes: Slide text:
Lord, you are my role model
Take away my self-centred life
Trace your pattern into my life
May all glory go to Jesus. Amen
Key points:
1. Lead the congregation in praying aloud together, in a quiet and warm tone.
2. Content of the prayer: confess building our house on sand, ask the Lord to dig the foundation deep, ask for the Holy Spirit’s guidance.
3. Prayer of resolve: Jesus is the role model I will follow all my life.
4. Blessing: all through today, may we lift up our eyes and see no one but Jesus.

brief21.title: Jesus Is My Role Model
notes: Slide text:
Kingdom 321 · The First of the Three Foundations
“For I have given you an example,
that you should also do as I have done to you.”

1. Greet the congregation and explain that today we come to the first of the Three Foundations.

3. Key verse: John 13:15; supporting verses Philippians 2:5 and Matthew 7:24.
4. Set the tone: Jesus is not only Saviour but role model.

brief21.title: Introduction (1) · A Leaning Tower
notes: Slide text:
The Pisa bell tower, begun in 1173
It began to lean at the third storey
The foundation was only about 3 metres deep
Beneath it lay soft clay and fine sand
Key points:
1. Construction began in August 1173; the marble gleamed white and the whole city was proud of it.
2. The cause of the lean was not the carving or the materials, but the foundation.
3. For over 800 years: grouting, counterweights, drawing out soil; closed in 1990, reopened in 2001.
4. All that engineering dealt with one thing: a foundation not properly laid in the first place.

brief21.title: Introduction (2) · Two Foundations
notes: Slide text:
Above ground: tall and handsome
Below ground: only three metres deep
“Everyone who hears these words of mine, and does them …
built his house on a rock.” (Matthew 7:24)
Key points:
1. Application: we can sing, pray and serve, yet the foundation is shallow.
2. The two foundations of Matthew 7:24–27: both men heard the same words and met the same storm.
3. The difference is not in the hearing but in the doing; the rock is not how many sermons I have heard but how much I have lived out.
4. The lean didn’t happen in a day; it started at the third storey.

brief21.title: Key Verse and Background
notes: Slide text:
The night before Passover, Jesus washes the disciples’ feet
He lays aside his garments and wraps a towel around his waist
He uses his authority to serve, not to press down
Example = a demonstration set before your eyes
Key points:
1. John’s Gospel was written by the apostle John around AD 80–90, probably in Ephesus.
2. Chapters 1–12 are “the Book of Signs,” chapters 13–21 “the Book of Glory”; chapter 13 is the turning point.
3. John 13:3–5; foot-washing was a slave’s job, and the disciples had just argued about who was greatest (Luke 22:24).
4. Original language: ὑπόδειγμα, a demonstration set before your eyes; 1 Peter 2:21 uses ὑπογραμμός, a copybook for tracing.
5. Background to Philippians: written by Paul around AD 60–62 while imprisoned in Rome, to a church troubled by rivalry and discord.

brief21.title: 1.1 Experience Is Precious but Subjective
notes: Slide text:
Elijah calls down fire on Carmel
Soon after, he asks to die under a juniper tree
Yesterday’s fire can’t burn up today’s fear
Key points:
1. 1 Kings 18:39, the people fell on their faces crying, “Yahweh, he is God!”; 19:4, he asked Yahweh to take away his life.
2. The lesson: some people’s faith is shaken because they meet a kind of suffering they have never been through before.
3. Psychology: Loftus and Palmer’s 1974 study — the wording of a question changed speed estimates, and people even remembered broken glass they never saw.
4. The sand-dune image: it looks like ground, but it moves.

brief21.title: 1.2 Tradition Has Value but Is Not Always Right
notes: Slide text:
“You set aside the commandment of God,
and hold tightly to the tradition of men” (Mark 7:8)
Tradition is not the enemy
Putting tradition where Jesus belongs is
Key points:
1. 2 Thessalonians 2:15, hold the traditions you were taught; tradition itself has value.
2. Mark 7:8 and 7:13: making void the word of God by your tradition.
3. The Pharisees were the most earnest and devout of all, yet did not recognise the Son of God standing in front of them.
4. The lesson: some churches are so bound by tradition that they miss God’s fresh leading.

brief21.title: 1.3 Jesus Alone Is the Unshakeable Rock
notes: Slide text:
“No one can lay any other foundation
than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.”
(1 Corinthians 3:11)
From the temporary perspective to the eternal
Key points:
1. 1 Corinthians 10:4, the rock was Christ; John 1:1, in the beginning was the Word.
2. Hebrews 13:8, the same yesterday, today and forever.
3. Hebrews 12:2: “author” is ἀρχηγός, the commander leading in front; “perfecter” is τελειωτής, the one who brings a thing to completion.
4. The 321 shift of perspective: from man’s to God’s, from the earthly to the heavenly, from the temporary to the eternal, from the worldly to the godly.
5. Ask: if all experiences and forms were taken away, what would I have left?

brief21.title: 2.1 The Life of Jesus Is the Pattern of the New Self
notes: Slide text:
Put away the old self of your former way of life
Be renewed in the spirit of your mind
And put on the new self (Ephesians 4:22–24)
The new self is created in the likeness of God
Key points:
1. Ephesians 4:20–24; “put away” and “put on” are the verbs of changing clothes.
2. The key is in the middle: be renewed in the spirit of your mind. Change the mindset and you change the life.
3. Changing behaviour without changing the mindset is suppression, not renewal.
4. The image of God is seen in Jesus: Colossians 1:15, Hebrews 1:3, John 1:14.
5. Romans 8:29, predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son.

brief21.title: 2.1 Copy the Original — Jesus — Every Day
notes: Slide text:
Painters don’t learn masterpieces by imagining
They set up their easels before the original
And copy it day after day
So must we copy Jesus every day
Key points:
1. Since the late eighteenth century the Louvre has run a copyists’ programme, with painters working in front of the originals.
2. 1 Peter 2:21: “leaving you an example” — in the original, a copybook for schoolchildren to trace.
3. Science: Bandura’s 1961 Bobo doll experiment; his 1977 Social Learning Theory argued that most human behaviour is learned by observing models.
4. Meltzoff and Moore, Science (1977): infants only 12 to 21 days old can imitate.
5. Rizzolatti’s team at the University of Parma discovered mirror neurons in the early 1990s.

brief21.title: 2.2 Take My Yoke, Learn from Me
notes: Slide text:
“For I am gentle and humble in heart;
take my yoke upon you, and learn from me”
(Matthew 11:29)
Disciple = someone still learning from him
Key points:
1. Read the whole of Matthew 11:28–30; my yoke is easy and my burden is light.
2. Original language: “learn from me”; μανθάνω and μαθητής share a root.
3. In rabbinic language, “yoke” meant the yoke of the Law; the picture of two oxen under one yoke, with the Lord up front carrying the weight.
4. In the first century, following a rabbi meant living with him; the Sayings of the Fathers urges sitting in the dust of the feet of the wise.
5. Mark 1:17, “Come after me” — not taking a course, but following him.

brief21.title: 2.2 As I Have Loved You, Love One Another
notes: Slide text:
The standard of the new commandment is Jesus himself
Love, forgiveness, humility, obedience, mercy
This is the DNA of God’s system
Key points:
1. John 13:34–35: not merely “love one another,” but “just as I have loved you.”
2. DNA isn’t on the surface, yet decides what every cell becomes; you can copy a programme sheet, but not the DNA.
3. Galatians 5:22–23, the ninefold fruit of the Spirit.
4. The 920 practice: everyone I relate to is my “2”; before them I live out the selfless “0” and bear the ninefold fruit, the “9.”
5. That night Jesus also washed Judas’s feet.

brief21.title: 2.3 Have the Mind of Christ Jesus
notes: Slide text:
“Who, existing in the form of God,
didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant”
(Philippians 2:6–7)
Key points:
1. Read the whole of Philippians 2:5–11; φρονέω is the orientation of the mind — precisely a change of mindset.
2. The staircase going down: not grasping, emptying himself, the form of a servant, the likeness of men, humbling himself, obedient to death, death on a cross.
3. ἁρπαγμός means a prize or privilege to be clutched and held on to.
4. Make it clear: emptying himself does not mean emptying out his deity, but not treating equality with God as a privilege to enjoy for himself.
5. The cross was the most shameful death, which the Romans reserved for slaves and rebels.

brief21.title: 2.3 Two Roads: Grasping Up, Walking Down
notes: Slide text:
Satan: I will make myself like the Most High
(Isaiah 14:14)
Jesus: didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped
Humility overcomes pride; selflessness overcomes Satan
Key points:
1. The five “I will”s of Isaiah 14:13–14, climbing all the way up.
2. 321: pride is leaving our originally intended position and grasping power, wanting to replace God; humility is laying down power and returning to our originally intended position.
3. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win.
4. The outcome: Philippians 2:9, “Therefore God also highly exalted him”; the one who walks downward is lifted up.
5. A line generally attributed to Bonhoeffer’s The Cost of Discipleship: “When Christ calls a man, he bids him come and die.”

brief21.title: 3.1 The Warning of the Bronze Serpent
notes: Slide text:
The bronze serpent God commanded brought healing
Seven hundred years later it had become an idol
Hezekiah broke it in pieces
(2 Kings 18:4)
Key points:
1. Numbers 21:8–9: the bronze serpent was commanded by God himself, and whoever looked at it lived.
2. 2 Kings 18:4: the Israelites were still burning incense to it, so Hezekiah broke it in pieces.
3. The bronze serpent itself had not changed; the human heart had.
4. An object God once used, once it is put in God’s place, becomes an idol that has to be smashed.

brief21.title: 3.2 Don’t Chase People or Miracles
notes: Slide text:
Taken for gods, Paul and Barnabas tore their clothes
“You seek me … because you ate of the loaves”
(John 6:26)
Key points:
1. Acts 14:14–15: we also are men of like passions with you.
2. Revelation 19:10, the angel said: Don’t do it! Worship God.
3. John 6:26: it is easy to fall in love with the bread in God’s hand rather than with God himself.
4. Psychology: Asch’s conformity experiments in the early 1950s; Milgram’s obedience-to-authority experiments at Yale in the early 1960s.
5. 1 Corinthians 1:12–13: Is Christ divided?

brief21.title: 3.3 No One but Jesus
notes: Slide text:
Peter wanted to build three tents
God said: This is my beloved Son; listen to him
“Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one,
except Jesus alone.” (Matthew 17:8)
Key points:
1. Matthew 17:1–8, the Mount of Transfiguration; building three tents put Moses and Elijah on a level with the Son of God.
2. Matthew 17:5, the voice from the cloud: listen to him.
3. The mark of maturity: when the cloud lifts, you look up and see no one but Jesus.
4. The lesson’s three lines: don’t let ministry models, leaders’ styles or spiritual experiences replace Jesus.
5. 321: Jesus is the focal point — not ourselves, not other people, not our circumstances.

brief21.title: Putting It into Practice (1)
notes: Slide text:
Read the Gospels daily
Watch what Jesus does; write down one aspect of his pattern
In conflict, ask: what would Jesus do?
Not ruled by instinct, but guided by his example
Key points:
1. The four Gospels have 89 chapters; read one a day and walk through Jesus’ whole life in three months.
2. Three notebook lines: Today I saw Jesus … I usually … Today I will …
3. Charles Sheldon’s In His Steps (1896), the source of WWJD.
4. Reminder: compare with the Gospels; don’t guess from imagination.
5. Every time you choose to be like Jesus, a little more of God’s system is built.

brief21.title: Putting It into Practice (2)
notes: Slide text:
Remind one another with a spiritual companion
Not living for ourselves, but living like Jesus
Eight stages: Information, Revelation, Conviction,
Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication
Key points:
1. 235 relationships: first a “2,” then a “3,” and then becoming a “5.”
2. Ask each other three questions each week: In what was I like Jesus? In what was I not? In which relationship will I practise next week?
3. 1 Corinthians 11:1, be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.
4. Repetition: Lally’s team (2010) found a new habit takes 66 days on average, ranging from 18 to 254 days.
5. Multiplication: 2 Timothy 2:2, commit these things to faithful people who will be able to teach others.

brief21.title: Summary: The 3-2-1 Vision
notes: Slide text:
Three Foundations, Two Core Values, the Goal
The old self is self-centred; the new self is selfless
Life first, then relationships, then ministry
According to the pattern shown on the mountain (Hebrews 8:5)
Key points:
1. Hebrews 8:5 and Exodus 25:40: building must follow the pattern.
2. The fivefold change: mindset, life, daily living, relationships, ministry.
3. The order of relationships: first with God, then with ourselves, then with others, and last with things; John 13:3, Jesus first knew that he came from God.
4. The Path of Serving: Spirit, Understanding, Life, Service, God.
5. The Goal: establish God’s system, letting Jesus be King and receive all the glory.

brief21.title: Closing and Call
notes: Slide text:
Jesus is not only Saviour but role model
Not only the starting point, but the model
Set your heart: follow Jesus all your life
Let Jesus be King and receive all the glory
Key points:
1. Take him only as Saviour and we live as a forgiven old self; take him as role model and we live as a renewed new self.
2. Return to the opening: the tower’s foundation could not be laid again, but our lives can.
3. Quote John 13:15 again and call people to set their hearts.
4. At home, at work, when misunderstood — he is still my role model.
5. What people recognise is not us, but Jesus.

brief21.title: Prayer of Response and Blessing
