“in whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.” (Ephesians 2:22)
practices: In every small decision, choose 321 principles
Before each day ends, look back in your devotional time
prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank you. You did not leave us in Babylon; you called us out. Nor did you abandon us in the wilderness; you want to build your own system in us.

Lord, shine your light on us and let us see which corners within us are still running the Babylonian way — the thoughts that want to make our own name great, the choices in small things where we indulge ourselves again and again.

Lord Jesus, we are willing to let you be King, and willing to let you receive all the glory. Be our role model all our lives; may your word be our standard day by day, and may the Holy Spirit be our guide moment by moment.

Give us grace to choose you in every small decision. When we fall, hold us up with your hand and help us stand and walk on; make our training become habit, our habit become a system, and our system become life, so that people may see your glory in us.
Let your Kingdom come; let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In the holy name of the Lord Jesus Christ we pray. Amen.
discussion: Revelation 18:4: “I heard another voice from heaven, saying, ‘Come out of her, my people, that you have no participation in her sins, and that you don’t receive of her plagues.’” Be specific: in your life right now (at work, at home, at school or online), which area is the place where you are most easily assimilated into the “Babylonian system”? This week, what “321 choice” are you willing to settle on for that area?

Daniel 1:8: “But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s dainties, nor with the wine which he drank. Therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.” Daniel couldn’t change his environment, but he could set a boundary in his heart. Share a time when you held your ground in your faith under pressure, or a time you wish you could do over. What did you learn from it about how God’s system is established through “falling, getting up and choosing again”?

blog.title: Which City Are You Building?

blocks.x: Coming out of Babylon is not moving house; it is switching systems
Morning Devotion 321 · Lesson 7 · Establish God’s System

Think back to yesterday. When someone claimed the credit for your work, what was your first reaction inside? When someone in your family said something cutting, did you choose to answer back, or to stay quiet?

Each of these things is small — so small that we would never write them down in our prayer journal. But here is a spiritual secret: you don’t decide which kingdom you belong to in one great battle; you hand yourself over to one kingdom or the other through a thousand small choices.

In The City of God, Augustine wrote: two loves have made two cities; love of self, even to the contempt of God, made the earthly city; love of God, even to the contempt of self, made the heavenly city. Two loves, two cities — this is the single thread that runs through the Bible from Genesis to Revelation.
Babylon Is Not a City; It Is a System
The name Babylon first appears as Babel in Genesis 11: “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves.” (Genesis 11:4)

Let’s build ourselves; let’s make a name for ourselves — this is the DNA of the Babylonian system, what 321 calls the self-centred life. Today’s Babylon has no gates of glazed brick, but it takes more refined forms: the scoring system that measures a person by performance, looks and the number of likes; the rhythm of life that, without your noticing, puts God in the very last slot of your diary.

So God’s call is: “Come out of her, my people, that you have no participation in her sins, and that you don’t receive of her plagues.” (Revelation 18:4) Notice the words “my people”: a person can already be saved and still think in the patterns of Babel.

But “coming out” alone is not enough. The Lord Jesus said that when the unclean spirit returned to the house it had left, it found it “empty, swept, and put in order,” and the last state of that man became worse than the first. An empty house cannot be held; you can’t just clear out — you must move in.
A System Is the Accumulation of Countless Choices

Daniel shows us the way. Taken captive into the Babylonian palace in his teens, he was given new surroundings, a new name, a new education and a new diet. He could not change Babylon, but inside it he could draw a line: “But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s dainties, nor with the wine which he drank.” (Daniel 1:8) The Hebrew behind “purposed” literally means “to set it upon the heart” — God’s system is established starting from the heart.

And under the ban that led to the lions’ den, he still prayed three times a day, “as he did before.” When the crisis came, he didn’t need to decide whether to pray, because he had decided long before. That is the power of a system.

In 2010 a team led by the University College London psychologist Phillippa Lally found that it takes an average of sixty-six days for a behaviour to become automatic — and that missing an occasional day does not significantly damage the formation of the habit. One slip will not destroy your system; only giving up will.

In 2012 Karen Adolph’s team at New York University video-recorded toddlers learning to walk and found that they take on average about 2,368 steps an hour and fall about seventeen times — and that the ones who fell most learned fastest. The Bible said it long ago: “for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again.” (Proverbs 24:16) True failure is not falling down, but refusing to get up again.
Three Exercises, Starting Tomorrow Morning

First, every morning, settle on one “321 choice”: Today, am I willing to let Jesus be King? Willing to let Jesus receive the glory? Will I take the Bible as my standard, Jesus as my role model and the Holy Spirit as my guide?
Second, in every small decision, choose 321: when emotions rise, let the Holy Spirit guide; when conflict comes, let Jesus be King; when temptation comes, let the Bible decide.

Third, before each day ends, look back: At what moment did I not let Jesus be King? Where did I seek my own glory? Reflection is not condemnation, but repentance and renewal; to turn back is to build again.

And remember: this is not by willpower but by grace. Philippians 2:13 says: “For it is God who works in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.” God is not standing on the shore shouting encouragement; God is the engine running inside us.
Revival is not a firework; revival is a furnace. A firework needs lighting once; a furnace needs fuel added every day. It begins as training, then becomes habit, and finally becomes life.
Reflection question: if you laid out every small choice you made yesterday, would you be building God’s system, or a human kingdom?

The Goal: Come Out of Babylon
“Come out of her, my people”
Revelation 18:4
Morning Devotion 321 · Lesson 7
Key points:
• Greet, and explain that today is the final link of the 3-2-1 vision: the Goal.
• The Three Foundations and Two Core Values all ultimately serve to establish God’s system.
• Key verse: Revelation 18:4; supplement with Isaiah 48:20.
• One line to set the tone: coming out is not moving house; it is switching systems.

brief12.title: Two Cities, Two Ways of Life
notes: Slide text:
Two loves have made two cities
Love of self builds the earthly city
Love of God builds the heavenly city
Which one are you building each day?
Key points:
• Open with yesterday’s small decisions: credit taken, a cutting remark at home — what was your first reaction?
• Augustine, The City of God, Book 14, chapter 28: two loves have made two cities.
• Historical background: the fall of Rome in AD 410.
• Golden line: you don’t pick a side in one great battle; you hand yourself over through a thousand small choices.

brief12.title: Babylon Is a System, Not a City
notes: Slide text:
Babel: let’s build, let’s make a name for ourselves
Babylon: a worldly, man-centred system
“You also are built together”
Ephesians 2:22
Key points:
• Three key phrases in Genesis 11:4: let’s build ourselves, let’s make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered.
• The DNA of the Babylonian system is what 321 calls the self-centred life.
• Historical background: Nebuchadnezzar II (reigned 605–562 BC); Jerusalem fell in 586 BC.
• Contrast: Babylon says “I build”; the kingdom says “being built” (the passive voice of Ephesians 2:22).
• Psalm 127:1: “Unless Yahweh builds the house, they who build it labor in vain.”

brief12.title: We Come Out in Order to Build
notes: Slide text:
Leaving is not enough; we must establish
Leave the Three Foundations and Two Core Values
And we naturally fall back into the worldly system
Return to 321 daily, and we are establishing
Key points:
• Matthew 12:43–44: the house swept clean but “empty” — and the end is worse.
• The lesson’s words: the only way out is to establish God’s system, with Christ at its centre.
• The word “naturally”: a house gathers dust, a garden grows weeds; spiritual desolation is a stretch of time with no one keeping watch.
• Matthew 7:24–25: the difference between rock and sand lies below ground.

brief12.title: In Babylon, Living Out God’s Kingdom
notes: Slide text:
Daniel purposed not to defile himself
Daniel 1:8
The three friends: “But if not” — we will not worship
Praying three times a day, as he did before
Key points:
• Daniel was taken captive in 605 BC and given new surroundings, a new name, a new education and a new diet.
• The Hebrew behind “purposed” literally means “to set it upon the heart.” The system begins in the heart.
• Daniel 3:17–18, “But if not”: faith no longer centred on me.
• Daniel 6:10, “as he did before”: no need to decide in the crisis, because it was decided long before.
• William James, Principles of Psychology (1890): habit is the enormous flywheel of society.

brief12.title: The Key Lies in Every Choice

Indulge myself, or let Jesus be King?
Follow my feelings, or obey the Bible?
Display myself, or give the glory to the Lord?
Choices become habits; habits become a system
Key points:
• The lesson’s golden saying: choose once and it has an effect; choose countless times and it forms a system; let the system run long enough and it becomes life.
• Deuteronomy 30:19, Joshua 24:15: God calls people to choose.
• Luke 16:10: faithful in a very little.
• Phillippa Lally’s team, 2010: forming a habit takes 66 days on average; missing a day does no real damage.
• Illustration: rainwater carving a riverbed; myelin in the brain making well-travelled pathways ever faster.

brief12.title: Know · Do · Receive
